subject: tool:gdl-matching-analysis
value:
TWO HALVES OF ONE RUN-54 REPORT, MEASURED SEPARATELY AT 80d3d02c8, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS TRUE.

CONFIRMED: `Select-String` matches case-INSENSITIVELY unless `-CaseSensitive` is passed, so the suite-verdict grep every lane reaches for -- `'Ran |OK|FAILED'` -- matches `test_foo (...) ... ok` on the `OK` alternative, i.e. EVERY PASSING TEST LINE of a verbose run. Measured on `@("Ran 10 tests in 1s", "test_foo ... ok", "OK", "FAILED (errors=1)")`: 4 rows without `-CaseSensitive`, 3 with it. This lane hit it live on its own first gate run, where the graph suite's verbose output buried `Ran 496 tests` and `OK` under hundreds of `... ok` rows. Use `-CaseSensitive` and anchor (`'^Ran \d+ tests'`, `'^OK'`) whenever the pattern's letters are also ordinary English.

REFUTED: `Select-String` does NOT corrupt `$LASTEXITCODE` on a long python stream, and saying it does misnames the culprit. It buffers its whole input, so it never breaks the pipe. Measured on a 241-line stream: `python tools/gdl/nearmiss.py --min 0 | Select-String -Pattern 'fn_'` exits 0; so do the `-List` and `-Quiet` forms that look like they stop early; `| Select-String -Pattern 'zzz-no-match'` exits 0. What corrupts the code is a `Select-Object -First` ANYWHERE downstream -- the same stream through `| Select-String -Pattern 'fn_' | Select-Object -First 2` exits -1. AGENTS.md trap 6a is therefore UNCHANGED IN SCOPE: `-First` is the whole mechanism, and a Select-String in the middle of such a pipe is a bystander.
